body.statement: For every valid finite binary-rational encoding \(\mathfrak E\), the finite monotone primal-dual certificate algorithm using the explicit resolution schedule terminates. It performs at most \(MKN_{\mathrm{prior}}N_{\mathrm{state}}N_{\mathrm{quad}}\) interval transition evaluations at \(p_{\mathrm{cert}}\)-bit fractional precision, followed by a finite linear program with at most \(N_{\mathrm{prior}}\) policy columns and \(M\) scenario rows, and returns \(\underline V_{\varepsilon}\leq V\leq\overline V_{\varepsilon}\) with \(\overline V_{\varepsilon}-\underline V_{\varepsilon}\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}}\). Its eight-entry ledger separately bounds terminal regularization, score-box exit, Gaussian-tail truncation, Gaussian-cell quadrature, time-score-clock interpolation, prior-net discretization, oracle offsets, and outward rounding by \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}}/8\) each. The algorithm returns an attained net prior and a finite mixture of net Bayes policies with maximum diffusion scenario regret at most \(\overline V_{\varepsilon}\); for all sufficiently large \(n\), boundary-stable policy transfer yields a predictable \(\pi_n\) with \(\max_m r_{n,m}(\pi_n)\leq\overline V_{\varepsilon}+o(1)\).
body.justification: The finite input model, resolution schedule, stopping bound, interval precision, and separated errors make the multidimensional certificate independently reproducible from primitive scenario data.
body.gap: Baas, ter Schure, and van Rosmalen provide a scalar finite-horizon recursion, and Rosenblum, Fang, and Liu provide an approximate sparse enrichment program; those works inform the construction but do not certify this continuum minimax value or a response-adaptive policy mixture.
body.consumer: The certificate can be attached to recruitment tables used by rpact and to finite-stage decision rules used by interAdapt.

obligation.what_is_open: The asserted eight-part interval error ledger is not determined by the frozen certificate handle.
obligation.obstruction: The handle does not specify the boundary extension, the interval interpolation formulas, the Gaussian cell enclosures, or a proved consistency estimate with the displayed constants. Monotonicity and finiteness alone cannot imply the requested numerical width.
obligation.attempted: I verified termination of every explicitly finite loop, the advertised transition-count bound, and the regularization, score-tail, prior-net, and accumulated-rounding budgets. The remaining interpolation, quadrature, oracle-offset, and policy-evaluation bounds require missing algorithmic formulas and stability estimates.
obligation.partial_result:
The parts forced by the displayed formulas can be certified.  Put
\(a=2^{-r_\delta}=\eta_{\mathrm{cert}}\) and
\(\delta_{\mathrm{cert}}=a^2\).  The definition of \(r_\delta\) implies
\[
a\leq\frac{19\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}}}{32K},\qquad
Ha\leq\frac{\log19}{2},\qquad
a\leq\frac{(\log19)^2}
{8\log(64K/\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}})}.
\]
Since \(20-a^2\geq19\) and \(\log(1+x)\leq x\),
\[
\frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{shift}}(a^2,a)}2
\leq\frac{Ka}{19}\leq\frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}}}{32},
\]
and
\[
2K\exp\!\left\{
-\frac{(\log(20-a^2)-Ha)^2}{2a}\right\}
\leq\frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}}}{32}.
\]
Thus the proved terminal comparison spends at most
\(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}}/16\), in particular at most the advertised
\(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}}/8\).

The score-stack representation also gives
\[
\sup_{m,u}\Pr_m^u\!\left\{
\max_j\sup_{t\leq1}|X_j(t)|>R_{\mathrm{cert}}\right\}
\leq4K\exp\!\left\{
-\frac{(R_{\mathrm{cert}}-H)^2}{2}\right\}
=\frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}}}{32}.
\]
The dual regret functional is \(1\)-Lipschitz in the prior's \(\ell_1\)
distance, so the displayed prior net costs at most
\(r_{\lambda,\mathrm{cert}}=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}}/32\).
Finally all mesh cardinalities are finite positive integers.  There are at
most
\[
MKN_{\mathrm{prior}}N_{\mathrm{state}}N_{\mathrm{quad}}
\]
listed interval-transition evaluations, and
\[
MKN_{\mathrm{prior}}N_{\mathrm{state}}N_{\mathrm{quad}}
\,2^{-p_{\mathrm{cert}}}
\leq\frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}}}{512}
\]
for one unit of outward-rounding error per evaluation.  Hence these loops
terminate and the final finite linear program terminates.  What is not
derivable is that the unspecified interpolation and Gaussian-cell
operations enclose the true Bellman semigroup with the remaining advertised
budgets; that missing estimate is exactly the unresolved part of
\(\mathrm{thm:certified\text{-}dynamic\text{-}program}\).
